definitions.explanation: The form of a language as it is currently spoken and written, as opposed to classical or archaic forms. In Japanese studies, refers to modern Japanese as distinct from classical Japanese (古語).

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{現代語|げんだいご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{訳|やく}した→訳す：02319_yakusu⟧。
examples.english: I translated this classic into modern language.

examples.japanese: {現代語|げんだいご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{使|つか}われなく→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many expressions that are no longer used in modern language.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古文|こぶん}→古文：17172_kobun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧⟦{原文|げんぶん}→原文：20563_genbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{現代語|げんだいご}⟦{訳|やく}→訳：23537_yaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}する→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧。
examples.english: In classical literature class, we first read the original text and then check the modern language translation.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of ⟦{現代|げんだい}→現代：02722_gendai⟧ (modern era) + ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (language). Most commonly encountered in the context of Japanese education, where students study ⟦{古文|こぶん}→古文：17172_kobun⟧ (classical texts) and translate them into {現代語|げんだいご}. The term {現代語訳|げんだいごやく} (modern language translation) is especially common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現代語訳|げんだいごやく} (modern language translation)
- {現代語|げんだいご}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{訳|やく}す→訳す：02319_yakusu⟧ (to translate into modern language)
- {現代語|げんだいご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧ (meaning in modern language)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{古語|こご}→古語：12065_kogo⟧: archaic/classical language — the opposite of {現代語|げんだいご}
- ⟦{口語|こうご}→口語：12033_kougo⟧: colloquial/spoken language — modern spoken form as opposed to written form
